observation_summary: The Dfp.multiply(int x) method failed for integer inputs outside the range [0, RADIX), violating the contract of the FieldElement interface which expects support for any integer.
reasoning_summary: The fix implements a missing branch in the algorithm to handle cases where the input integer is outside the range supported by the existing 'multiplyFast' method. By delegating to the more general 'multiply(Dfp)' method when the input is out of range, the code now correctly fulfills the interface contract. This is a classic algorithmic correction to handle a broader set of inputs.
evidence_used: The bug report states that Dfp.multiply(int x) was limited to 0 <= n <= 9999, violating the FieldElement.multiply(int n) contract.
The fix adds an if-else block to check if the input x is within the range [0, RADIX), and if not, calls the general multiply(newInstance(x)) method.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix adds a conditional check, the primary purpose is to extend the functionality (the algorithm) to handle a wider range of inputs, not just to validate input for safety or error reporting.
The fix does not change the interface signature or the way modules communicate; it changes the internal implementation of a method to satisfy an existing interface contract.
